nodes.summary: If a multiset $s$ of natural numbers consists of $x_1, \dots, x_k$, listed with multiplicity, then the pairwise products of $s$ form the multiset of the products $x_i x_j$ over all pairs of indices $1 \le i < j \le k$; equal elements at different positions give separate products, and the result is empty when $k < 2$.
nodes.title: Pairwise products of a multiset

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $\lambda$ and $\mu$ be partitions of $n$ with a common largest part, that is, some $a$ is a part of both $\lambda$ and $\mu$ and no part of either exceeds $a$. If the pairwise products of the parts of $\lambda$ and the pairwise products of the parts of $\mu$ form the same multiset, then $\lambda = \mu$.
nodes.title: Li's lemma: reconstruction from the largest part and pairwise products

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $\lambda$ and $\mu$ be partitions of $n$. The pairwise products of the parts of $\lambda$ and the pairwise products of the parts of $\mu$ form the same multiset if and only if $\lambda = \mu$.
nodes.title: Li's theorem: partitions are determined by their pairwise products

inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved

stated.label: statement formalized
